title: Doughnut Emoji 🍩 Meaning: Sweet Snack, Zero and More
description: What 🍩 means: doughnuts and coffee runs, police jokes, a score of zero, car stunts and occasional innuendo. A guide to reading the doughnut emoji.
summary: The 🍩 doughnut emoji means doughnuts, breakfast treats and coffee runs. Its ring shape also lets it stand for zero, as in a scoreless game, and for spinning a car in circles. It appears in police jokes and Homer Simpson references, and is sometimes used as sexual innuendo.
meaning: A frosted ring with sprinkles is an instantly cheerful image, and most use of 🍩 is as simple as it looks. It is the emoji of morning treats: a box brought to the office, a stop on the way to school, a reward after a run. It pairs with coffee by default. In the United States, National Doughnut Day on the first Friday of June, when shops give away free ones, brings a yearly surge.

Two cultural jokes travel with it. One is the stereotype of police officers eating doughnuts, so 🍩 next to 👮 or 🚓 is a gentle jab at cops. The other is Homer Simpson, whose pink-frosted doughnut is among the best-known foods in television. People use the emoji to voice the same helpless craving. Spelling varies, with “donut” common in American usage, but the emoji serves both.

The hole matters too. In sports, “a doughnut” is a zero on the scoreboard, and fans use 🍩 to mock a team that failed to score or to praise a pitcher or goalkeeper for a shutout. Drivers “do doughnuts” by spinning a car in tight circles, which the emoji can also represent. And in sexual slang the ring can stand for an orifice, usually next to 🍆, a reading that needs a clearly suggestive setup.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Mostly it is about food and small kindnesses: “I brought 🍩” is a welcome thing to read in any group chat. It expresses cravings and cheat days. Friends may use it to tease someone who scored zero in a game or got no replies. Its default mood is light and generous.

contexts.label: In sports
contexts.body: Scoreboard talk uses it for nothing. A pitcher “hanging doughnuts” is putting up scoreless innings; a tennis set won 6-0 is closely related to a “bagel.” Fans post 🍩 after a shutout, either to celebrate their defense or to needle the opponent. Car and motorsport fans use it for celebratory spins after a race win.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It announces treats in the break room and softens Monday mornings. Team channels use it for birthdays and small wins. It is entirely safe professionally, with the mild exception of police humor, which may not land with everyone. As office currency, doughnuts rank just below pizza.

examples.text: Left a dozen in the kitchen, go go go 🍩
Coffee and a 🍩 kind of morning ☕
Seven innings of 🍩🍩🍩. Our ace is unreal
examples.meaning: Praising a pitcher for holding the other team scoreless.
A Homer Simpson-style expression of craving.
Spinning a car in circles for fun.

combos.meaning: Doughnuts and coffee, the classic morning pairing.
A joke about police officers and their supposed favorite snack.
A sexual reference, with the ring representing an orifice.
Doing doughnuts, spinning a car in circles.

confusedWith.difference: 🥯 is also a ring of dough, but it is savory, usually shown with cream cheese, and means breakfast or New York delis. In tennis, a 6-0 set is a bagel; the doughnut covers zeros in other sports.
🍪 is a flat chocolate-chip cookie. Both are sweet snacks, yet the cookie has internet and Christmas associations, while the doughnut's extras are cops, cars and zero.
⭕ is a plain red ring used for “correct” in Japan or to circle something. It is a symbol, not a food, even though both are circles with a hole.

avoid: Don't use cop-and-doughnut jokes with police officers you don't know or in serious discussions of policing.
Avoid pairing it with an eggplant unless you fully intend the sexual meaning.
design: The emoji shows a ring doughnut with glaze and multicolored sprinkles. Chocolate frosting is the most common choice among vendors, with some designs opting for pink icing that recalls the Simpsons version. Whether the doughnut is seen from above or at an angle differs, but all major platforms include the hole and the sprinkles.

faqs.a: Several things, by context. It can mean zero, especially a scoreless result in sports. It can mean spinning a car in circles. In sexual slang it stands for an orifice. Most of the time, though, it simply means a doughnut.

faqs.q: What does 🍩 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: Usually a snack craving, a coffee run or an offer to bring you something sweet. If it follows an eggplant or a clearly flirtatious line, it may be innuendo. On its own it is innocent.

faqs.q: Why are doughnuts associated with police?
faqs.a: In the mid-twentieth-century United States, doughnut shops were among the few places open late at night, so officers on overnight shifts stopped there. The image stuck in films and comedy, and the emoji is now used for the same joke.

Both are accepted. “Doughnut” is the traditional spelling and the emoji's official name; “donut” is a shortened form popular in the United States. Searching either word on an emoji keyboard usually brings up 🍩.

faqs.q: When was the doughnut emoji added?
faqs.a: It has been part of the standard emoji set since 2010, appearing with the other original desserts such as the cookie and chocolate bar.
